module_title: Introduction to Control, Waste, and Framework Systems
introduction: This section covers how our body thinks and coordinates (Nervous and Endocrine Systems), how it removes toxic waste (Excretory System), and what gives it shape and support (Skeletal System).

core_concepts.title: The Nervous System
core_concepts.description:
This is the body's 'Control Room', communicating via high-speed electrical signals. 
Basic Unit: **The Neuron (Nerve Cell)**. It is the 'longest cell' in the human body. 
Main Parts: The Brain and the Spinal Cord (Central Nervous System).

core_concepts.title: The Endocrine System
core_concepts.description:
This system controls the body slowly but over long periods using chemical messengers. 
Glands: Special organs that secrete chemicals called **Hormones**. 
Key Feature: They are 'Ductless' (meaning they have no tubes); they release their hormones directly into the 'Bloodstream'.

core_concepts.title: The Excretory System
core_concepts.description:
The system responsible for filtering out toxic wastes (like urea) from the blood and removing them as urine. 
Main Organ: **Kidneys**. 
Basic Unit: **The Nephron** (Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that act as microscopic filters).

core_concepts.title: The Skeletal System
core_concepts.description:
It provides a rigid framework, defines our shape, and protects vital internal organs (the skull protects the brain, ribs protect the heart). 
An adult human has exactly **206 bones** (a newborn baby has around 300, which fuse together as they grow).

important_entities.name: Filtration of Blood
important_entities.significance: Examiners often ask this: The Lungs 'Purify' the blood (by adding O2 and removing CO2), but the Kidneys 'Filter' the blood (by removing urea and nitrogenous waste).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Biggest Exam Trap: The names sound very similar. Always remember: 
- **Neuron**: The structural unit of the Nervous System (Brain). 
- **Nephron**: The structural filtering unit of the Excretory System (Kidney).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Endocrine glands secrete their hormones 'Inside' the blood directly, rather than through a duct or tube to the outside.

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed SSC/Railway question: 'Which is the longest cell in the human body?' Answer: The Nerve Cell (Neuron).
